title: Dietary cholesterol from eggs increases the ratio of total cholesterol to high-density lipoprotein cholesterol in humans: a meta-analysis
authors: Weggemans RM, Zock PL, Katan MB
population: 17 controlled trials with parallel or crossover design in which diets differed only in cholesterol or egg content and were fed for at least 14 days
funder: Supported by the Netherlands Heart Foundation (grant number 95.118).
authorConflicts: No conflict statement; the authors were affiliated with Wageningen University and the Wageningen Centre for Food Sciences.
result: 17 trials, 24 dietary comparisons, 556 subjects. Each additional 100 mg dietary cholesterol per day raised the ratio of total to HDL cholesterol by 0.020 (95% CI 0.010 to 0.030), total cholesterol by 0.056 mmol/L (0.046 to 0.065) and HDL cholesterol by 0.008 mmol/L (0.005 to 0.010). Taking one egg as 200 mg cholesterol, one additional egg daily was predicted to raise LDL cholesterol by 0.100 ± 0.008 mmol/L and the total-to-HDL ratio by 0.041 ± 0.011. Per 100 mg, LDL cholesterol rose by 0.036 ± 0.004 mmol/L in studies with background diets low in saturated fat and by 0.061 ± 0.006 mmol/L with diets high in saturated fat (P = 0.03). Diet-induced changes vary considerably between individuals.
